svg.title: RIEMANN R4 — Families of definite unitary groups: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 4 in one poster: its 44 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-family-data-exists, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: This chapter proves thm-family-data-exists: if cuspidal representations of GL_a over CM fields have Galois representations, some class of families of definite unitary groups satisfies the family hypotheses. The zero-free region needs them: thm-zero-free-from-families takes such a class, together with the Tate–Shafarevich bound, and shows that primitive Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros right of 1/2. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

The zero-free region needs them: thm-zero-free-from-families takes such a class, together with the

A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)
Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines (four on a short card). The footer gives its file and
line in the mirror and the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges. A proof use outside the chapter is counted, not drawn. Rows: a card's row is one above the highest card whose proof uses it, or higher
where that makes room; a card sits under the cards that use it where it can. A short card shows four lines of the signature and one paragraph of the proof.

text.tspan: Lattice and depth estimates at the points of a family

svg.text: Suppose that the basic size conditions hold at the points of the families: bounds on the size, the
scale, the bad primes, the level and a parameter Y, and agreement of the error constant with its
definition. Then at every point at a large scale, and for every large enough constant c: the
lattices M_j are full and stable under the finite group that acts on them, and the lattices
attached to the archimedean places are full;
The height inequalities of prop-height-inequalities-at-points hold along the family.
They give the fullness and stability of the lattices, and with the size conditions they give the
index bound at pairs of places.
For the depth bounds, pass to the points of the integral model of a unitary Shimura variety.

place. Then the families built from p satisfy the membership conditions.

text.tspan: Periods and valuations at the good data

svg.text: For any construction data and any choice of admissible data, the following six conditions hold
at the good data of the families, for all large auxiliary fields: on the reference lattice chain of
each member the period map is injective, the stabiliser maps are bijective, and the periods are
rational, integral, and bounded by the majorants of the lattices;
The good data lie over standard constructions. Each of the six conditions is proved at the
points of standard constructions and then carried to the good data. The sixth is
Proof uses lem-valuations-level-primes · 1 of these are not drawn here
For any construction data built from a system of local parameters (def-local-parameters),

text.tspan: The basic conditions hold for the families from local

svg.text: Fix a system of local parameters (def-local-parameters) and a real constant c. Build the
families of definite unitary groups from the construction data that these parameters and c
determine. Then, for all large auxiliary fields, the twelve basic conditions hold at every
admissible datum of these families: primitivity, the λ' condition, the divisor condition,
decomposition points, selection jumps, compatibility conditions, labels, goodness, weak
geometric compatibility, multiplicities, the κ condition and the defect condition.
We take the twelve conditions in groups; each group follows from a few published results.
Primitivity and decomposition points hold by construction of the data.
Compatibility conditions come from the existence of the Weil representation of unitary dual
pairs, Harish-Chandra's finiteness theorem, the theory of discrete series and the rapid decay
of cusp forms. With primitivity and decomposition points they also give the selection jumps.
The multiplicity condition is the isometric period identity of
prop-isometric-period-identity, which rests on unramified Howe duality, the
Siegel–Weil formula, the doubling method and strong approximation. The same results give

text.tspan: 3 · The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….
This section defines the objects of the chapter. A member of a family (def-family-member)
is built from rank data (def-family-ranks), archimedean parameters (
def-harish-chandra-parameters) and hermitian spaces over an auxiliary CM field: a
definite chain with intermediate, indefinite and auxiliary spaces (
def-family-hermitian-spaces). Scales and size data (def-family-scale) fix the weights
of a member, and a family (def-family) is a set of members, one set for each scale, that
covers all weights. def-family-data lists the family hypotheses, the conditions on a class of
families that the rest of the chapter proves.

text.tspan: 2. Members, Siegel masses and admissible data

svg.text: This is the first step of the proof of thm-family-data-exists: we build the members of the
families from a system of local parameters and find admissible data at their points. The key
theorem, thm-family-membership-admissible-data, gives a ratio of Siegel masses of
standard hermitian lattices, the membership conditions and the admissible data. Its proof
builds partial constructions of depth three and four, passes twice through them, and gets the
twisting property at constructed points from theta series. One input, the equality of cuspidal
multiplicities on inner forms (thm-inner-form-multiplicities-equal), comes from a

text.tspan: 3. Local estimates at the points of a family

svg.text: This is the second step of the proof of thm-family-data-exists. At the points of a family,
thm-twisting-index-and-archimedean-bounds bounds the index of the standard lattices
in the lattices M_j at the twisting places and bounds the archimedean weights below. Height
inequalities and integral models of unitary Shimura varieties bound the depth of the local data
prop-lattice-and-depth-estimates), and explicit exponents bound the twists at the
twisting places (prop-exponent-bounds-twisting-places). The definite-side condition of
thm-family-conditions-from-basic and the slope bound on the indefinite side use the
This is the third step of the proof of thm-family-data-exists. For the families built from a
system of local parameters, thm-basic-conditions-from-local-parameters shows that
twelve basic conditions hold at every admissible datum. Most hold by construction or follow
from a few published results. The multiplicity condition is the isometric period identity of
prop-defect-condition) is a norm bound on the definite side. The next section derives the
full list of family conditions from these twelve.

text.tspan: 5. The full list of family conditions

svg.text: This is the sixth step of the proof of thm-family-data-exists.
thm-family-conditions-from-basic derives the 26 family conditions from the twelve basic
ones, the covolume condition and the functional condition. Four propositions do most of the
work: periods and valuations behave at the good data (
prop-periods-valuations-good-data); the small terms, the off-diagonal bound and the
level bound hold (prop-small-terms-offdiag-level); the chosen data serve their families
(prop-chosen-data-serve-families); and the counting constants and constituents are
off-diagonal bound and the counting theorem behind them are proved in chap-theta.
